<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via bindAppArtifactHandlers (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2c0202f7ea11ef8ff1397ff23dadf5d58d45fc8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `88defac24dd3001e0a9309f418edac6e9dddf0dc` — the merge of head `73ef5d90fc2db6cd9781fbcd8b1ece0a3d9d76f3` into base `b2c0202f7ea11ef8ff1397ff23dadf5d58d45fc8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 88defac24dd3001e0a9309f418edac6e9dddf0dc && git checkout 88defac24dd3001e0a9309f418edac6e9dddf0dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b2c0202f7ea11ef8ff1397ff23dadf5d58d45fc8 73ef5d90fc2db6cd9781fbcd8b1ece0a3d9d76f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro b2c0202f7ea11ef8ff1397ff23dadf5d58d45fc8 && git merge --no-ff 73ef5d90fc2db6cd9781fbcd8b1ece0a3d9d76f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2c0202f7ea11ef8ff1397ff23dadf5d58d45fc8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b2c0202f7ea11ef8ff1397ff23dadf5d58d45fc8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8c9a7da49492d1f9eb6ab2015568bc49f46cd7f2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts

Round 1, PR #32333, card #32245. Inputs: the card body and its three comments (triage 6770721852, claim 6775326490, os-dev-report 6777393480), the PR body, its 10-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Code outside the diff was read in the tree at this head, never reviewed.

Check-runs on this head as read (64 runs): 21 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 32 `in_progress`, 0 failed. Concluded green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate. NOT concluded at read time: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, the two scoped lints, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build & E2E UI, Type Check UI, Live E2E UI. This record judges the contract; it certifies no gate that had not concluded. The landing check (every check green) is still owed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`composeStacks` accept set, widened: right.** Under `manifest: 'preserve'`, a key declared by two or more inputs is admitted when it is the object-less key (`global:NAME`, embedded by no object), every declaring input is one package (a `manifest.id`, no `packages` list), no two share an id, and no two meet under `namespacedHoldersMeet`. That is the install gate's rule for the same pair (`SchemaRegistry.bareNameHoldersOtherThan` reads `manifest.namespace` off the installed record; compose reads `stack.manifest.namespace`): one field, one predicate. Compose is stricter in two places and both fail closed: an input keyed by `manifest.name` with no `id` is refused (the boot keys `id || name`), and one package id twice is refused (install treats a re-register as no new holder).
2. **Still refused, as the card requires: right.** One namespace, two bodies of one package, a package with no namespace, the default manifest (`'last'`, `'first'`, an index) and every object-bound key keep `STACK_COMPOSE_ACTION_KEY_COLLISION`. The shareable namespaces `base` / `system` / `sys` follow the install gate exactly: two packages of one of them meet (refused), a pair across two of them does not.
3. **Refusal text: right.** The error's `lines` payload is unchanged; the message gains one sentence only when a refused key would be admitted under `preserve`. See nit N1.
4. **New public export `namespacedHoldersMeet` (`@objectstack/spec/kernel`): right.** Additive; `api-surface/kernel.json` and `export-origins/kernel.json` carry it. `collectComposedActionKeyCollisions` and `formatComposedActionKeyCollisions` change signature but are `@internal` and unexported.
5. **`bareNameHoldersMeet` (objectql): accept set unchanged.** The expression moved is character for character the one it replaces; the type test still runs first.
6. **Binder owner change (runtime): right in direction, one hole.** For a bundle carrying `packages[]`, each body's actions are registered under `app:PACKAGE_ID` where they were all under `app:ARTIFACT_ID`. That is ADR-0150 D4's key (`(package, objectName, name)`), it matches `actionHandlerCoordinate` (`app:ID` maps to the package coordinate) and `artifactPackageId` is the key `registerApp` installs under. It moves three observable things: a package-qualified call reaches a non-artifact-id package's handler (the declared fix), `listRegisteredActions().package` reads the body's owner (declared), and any `OBJECT:NAME` two bodies carry is now held under two package coordinates, so a call that names no package is refused 409. The third is the card's pin for the object-less pair and is unpinned for every other way two bodies carry one key: finding F1.
7. **The install-local door moves too.** `MarketplaceInstallLocal` binds through the same function and accepts `packages[]` bundles, so its owners change the same way. The changeset names `AppPlugin` only (nit N3).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/32245-compose-object-less-action-per-namespace.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`; all three are packages the diff moves and no moved package is missing. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` by AGENTS.md step 3, and by the rule's letter `none` holds: no key, accepted value or metadata type is added. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; Check Changeset and the PR-body guards concluded `success`.

Clause-②: yes (widening) is the right arm for the compose half. It is complete only if F1 measures clean: if the reconciled-object case below answers 409 where base ran a handler, the diff also narrows and the line owes that arm.

For the seat, not a finding: #31973 declared `Metadata-protocol: added` (`minor`) for the same class of change at the install door (a second holder accepted for agent and skill). The claim on this card declared `none` and the dev copied it, as os-dev requires. The two readings of one class of change now sit side by side on `main`'s history.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relayed-author note is owed.
- Dev flag, "hooks and functions of a multi-package artifact are still bound under the artifact's owner (NOT MEASURED)": pre-existing, in neither card pin, correctly left alone. It is now asymmetric with actions in one module, and the module header says so. Escalated: it has `carrier: none`; the seat files a card or records why not.
- Dev flag, "`resolveArtifactCollections` keys every item by name, so two bodies' same-named items of other families resolve to one": pre-existing and that module's documented rule. Read at this head, the binder is the only runtime reader that binds from `collectBundleActions`; the CLI's own readers (`packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts`) were not examined by the dev or here. Escalated with the first: `carrier: none`.
- Dev flag, "a nested multi-package artifact as an input has its bodies' actions unwalked (NOT MEASURED)": confirmed by reading. Step 6 walks each input's top-level `actions`, and a stripped `preserve` artifact carries none, so composing such an artifact with a third package that declares the same object-less name sees one declaring stack and admits it whatever the third package's namespace. The same hole exists on base for every action key, so this diff does not open it; `composedPackagesHoldApart` refuses a nested artifact only when its own top level declares the key. Escalated: `carrier: none`, and this one is a compose door admitting what the install gate refuses, so it should not stay unfiled.
- Dev deviation, "the bare 409 names both packages, not the `/actions/NS/global/NAME` URLs": the card's pin is "the bare call gives 409 naming both". Met; the text is #32213's.
- Dev deviation, no assignee or reviewer set: os-dev rule 2. Accepted.
- Card line "Epic red-line review before landing": not this record's. Still owed by the epic seat.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts` (hits): holds.** `namespacedHoldersMeet` is the install gate's expression, moved, and both doors now read the one copy. Its jsdoc sentences check against the tree: a package with no namespace meets every holder; co-owners and the shareable namespaces meet; "which types narrowed, and that two bodies of one package are one holder, stay with each door" is true of both callers. A pure predicate beside the existing namespace rules is consistent with what the module already holds. No finding.

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (hits): holds against the card and ADR-0150 D2/D4, with one stale sentence (in F1) and N1.** Tried and held: three or more holders (pairwise); a third package of a present namespace; a no-namespace or non-string namespace (reads as none, meets); an input with `packages: []` (refused); an object named `global` (`embeddedKeys` excludes it); two byte-identical action bodies (the multiset reproduction test still strips); the additive shape (a manifest-less third input keeps the flattened `actions` with both entries, and the binder's residual is keyed `OBJECT:NAME`, so neither is bound a third time). Step 8 strips the flattened copy only when the bodies reproduce it, so the widened artifact is emitted in a shape the boot's per-body read covers.

**`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts` (implementing): agrees.** No finding.

**`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` (implementing): agrees for the card's scenario; F1, N2.**

Findings:

- **F1 · should-fix · the binder now reads unreconciled bodies, and a reconciled object is unpinned.** `actionBindingGroups` reads each `packages[]` body alone. On base the binder read `resolveArtifactCollections(bundle)`, which takes the composed top level first, and `composeStacks` keeps that top level exactly when the bodies do not reproduce it (`packagesReproduceComposedCollections`: `objectConflict: 'merge'` or `'override'`). Take two packages that both declare object `o` with an embedded action `x` (legal: step 6 attributes an object's embedded actions to one stack, so it reports no collision; reachable for co-owners of one namespace or packages with no namespace). Base bound `o:x` once, the reconciled body, under one coordinate. This head binds alpha's `o:x` under `app:alpha` and beta's under `app:beta`. By `ActionsFacet.unqualifiedHandler` (two packages hold a handler under one key, on any object) a call that names no package then answers 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` where base ran the reconciled handler, and under `'override'` the body the composition replaced is live again at its package's coordinate. NOT MEASURED: read from the tree under the read-only rule, including whether the boot's registration admits both bodies' `o`. The hits file states the opposite premise in step 6's doc ("Under `objectConflict: 'override'` the other stacks' embedded declarations on that object are not in the artifact at all"), which is no longer true of a `preserve` artifact at the boot. Owed: a pin that boots a `preserve` artifact composed with `'override'` (and `'merge'` with identical embedded actions) and reads the bare call and both coordinates; then either bind only what the reconciled artifact carries for a key two bodies share, or declare the 409 as a `(narrowing)` and correct the sentence. A delta review of the fix is owed.
- **N1 · nit · the `preserve` sentence can overstate.** `preserveWouldAdmit` is set when any one refused key would be admitted, so a refusal that also lists a key `preserve` would still refuse (an object-bound key, a one-namespace pair) ends with "To keep both object-less actions, compose with { manifest: 'preserve' }", and "both" is wrong for three holders. Message text only.
- **N2 · nit · the module's own prose now understates the owners.** The header still opens "both under ONE owner, `app:appId`"; `appArtifactHandlerOwner`'s jsdoc says every handler bound for `appId` is registered under it; `AppArtifactHandlerBinding.owner` says "the owner key the handlers were registered under". The "Re-binding replaces, it never accumulates" paragraph does not say that the teardown walks the NEW bundle's groups only, so a package body a re-bind no longer carries keeps its `app:PACKAGE_ID` action handlers (NOT MEASURED; a member an install-local bundle drops may well stay installed, in which case keeping them is right, but the paragraph should say which).
- **N3 · nit · prose face, the lane seat's.** The changeset's Boot paragraph says `bindAppArtifactHandlers` is "used by `AppPlugin`"; the install-local door calls it too and its `packages[]` bundles change owner the same way.

Nits are fixed on the prose faces only, or left as accepted deviations; N1 lives in a hits file's emitted string, so fixing it moves the head and is best folded into F1's fix or a follow-up card.

**Epic red-line read — no PASS at `22b11016`** (#32245, compose and boot per namespace for object-less actions). One required fix, R1, which is a declaration only.

**What holds**
- **Compose.** It admits a key only when it is object-less (no `object:name` key and `global:` scope), every input stack is one package (`manifest.id`, no `packages`), no two share an id, and no pair meets under `namespacedHoldersMeet`. That is now one function, and the install gate's `bareNameHoldersMeet` calls it too. Every other shape is refused as before. Admission matches install, so nothing is admitted that install refuses, apart from #32335, which is filed.
- **Boot.**
  - `actionBindingGroups` binds a key one body holds under that body's `app:PACKAGE_ID`.
  - It splits a two-namespace object-less pair so that each body binds its own action objects.
  - A key two bodies hold any other way stays as one handler under the artifact owner, as before.
  - The bare call then reaches #32213's `pickActionHolder`, which refuses 409 naming both. Nothing is picked.
  - A re-bind removes every recorded owner.

**R1 (required): declare the narrowing that moving the handlers carries**

Before, every action of a multi-package artifact was registered under `app:ARTIFACT_ID`. A call qualified by the artifact's own id therefore reached every body's action: `executeAction` with `packageId: ARTIFACT_ID`, and `/actions/NS/...` where the artifact id resolves to a namespace (for example when the top-level id is also a body's id). Now only that body's own actions answer it, and another body's action answers 404 (or 409 not-held). That is a 200→404 move, so it is a narrowing. The changeset declares only the widening and carries no ADR-0087 marker.

Add to the changeset:
- the narrowing, with FROM (qualifying by the artifact's own id) TO (qualifying by the declaring package's id or namespace);
- the ADR-0087 marker;
